other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act

summary: The Ratepayer Protection Act requires state utility regulators and nonregulated electric utilities to consider adopting a federal standard regarding large-load electricity consumers, specifically data centers and similar facilities. The standard ensures these large customers pay the full cost of any electric system upgrades needed to serve them and provide upfront financial assurances.

affected_groups.effect: Non-residential electric consumers operating data centers or IT infrastructure with a peak demand of 100 megawatts or more must pay the full incremental costs of grid upgrades and provide financial assurances or contributions upfront before upgrades begin.
Must commence consideration of the federal standard within one year and make a final determination within two years, unless they previously implemented or considered a comparable standard.
affected_groups.group: State regulatory authorities and nonregulated electric utilities

affected_groups.effect: Must design rates to recover full upgrade costs from large-load customers and require financial assurances or contributions prior to executing any necessary generation, transmission, or distribution upgrades.

key_provisions: Requires state utility regulators and nonregulated utilities to consider a new federal standard for large-load customers within one year and complete determinations within two years.

Defines large-load customers as non-residential consumers using electricity primarily for information technology infrastructure, data storage, or computational services with a peak demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site or campus.
Mandates that electricity rates charged to large-load customers cover the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrades necessary to serve them.
Requires electric rates to cover upgrade costs even if the large-load customer terminates its contract or stops purchasing energy.
Requires electric utilities to collect financial assurances or contributions from large-load customers to cover upgrade costs before any utility upgrades are made.
Exempts utilities from the new consideration timeline if the state has already implemented, considered, or voted on a comparable standard prior to enactment.
missing_information: Specific financial penalties for states or utilities that fail to meet the consideration deadlines.
Details on how existing contracts entered into prior to enactment are handled, beyond the definition applying on or after the date of enactment.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Ratepayer Protection Act requires state utility regulators and nonregulated electric utilities to consider adopting a federal standard regarding large-load electricity consumers, specifically data centers and similar facilities. The standard ensures these large customers pay the full cost of any electric system upgrades needed to serve them and provide upfront financial assurances.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a formal federal ratemaking standard aimed at shifting the financial responsibility of grid upgrades away from general ratepayers and onto massive power users like data centers. The significance depends heavily on how individual states choose to implement or adopt the standard during their required proceedings.
